title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Data Re-uploading for EEG-based ADHD Classification
target_journal: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering / MDPI Technologies
executive_summary: A hybrid quantum-classical architecture for ADHD diagnosis from 19-channel EEG: a classical spatial-temporal backbone $f_{\phi}$ condenses each epoch into $d = N_q = 4$ features bounded to $[-\pi, \pi]$, and a parameterized quantum circuit with circular Data Re-uploading (DRU) over $L$ layers acts as an expressive non-linear classifier. The whole network is trained end-to-end with a subject-weighted binary cross-entropy, and analytical gradients through both stages give a channel-time saliency map for clinical audit.

novelty.problem_statement: Degraded subject-level classification accuracy of hybrid quantum-classical models with shallow data encodings on pediatric ADHD EEG.

pillars.name: Spatial-temporal EEG feature compression matching the qubit register
pillars.summary: $f_{\phi}: \mathbb{R}^{C \times T} \to [-\pi, \pi]^d$ with $d = N_q = 4$, bounded by a scaled hyperbolic tangent (Eq. 1).
pillars.details: One feature per qubit keeps the register small enough to measure its gradient variance directly (E3). The features are learned generically; whether they track Theta, Beta, the Theta/Beta ratio or frontal coherence is a post-hoc contrast, never imposed by the architecture.

pillars.name: L-layer circular-entanglement DRU circuit with Fourier expressivity of degree L
pillars.summary: $U(x, \theta, \beta) = \prod_{l=1}^{L} W_l(\theta_l) S_l(x, \beta_l)$ with $S_l = \bigotimes_j R_y(x_j + \beta_{l,j})$ en unit scale and a closed CNOT ring (Eqs. 2-5).
pillars.details: Every expectation value is a truncated Fourier series whose frequencies per feature are the integers $-L, \dots, L$; $\theta$, $\beta$ and the topology set its coefficients, never its frequencies. The ring entangles every bipartition of the register, though no 4-qubit state is maximally entangled across all of them.

pillars.name: Clinical interpretability via channel-time gradient saliency
pillars.details: Exact gradients through the classical and quantum stages (backpropagation in simulation, the parameter-shift rule on hardware) expose each electrode and time sample, to audit that the decision rests on fronto-central sites (Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, Fz, Cz) rather than noise.

hypotheses.title: Hybrid classification and Fourier expressivity
hypotheses.statement: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.

hypotheses.title: Entanglement topology ablation
hypotheses.statement: Circular CNOT entanglement, which entangles every bipartition of the 4-qubit register without making all of them maximally entangled at once, yields higher diagnostic discriminability than linear nearest-neighbor entanglement or separable single-qubit rotations.

hypotheses.title: Re-uploading depth and barren plateaus
hypotheses.statement: Expressivity in the accessible Fourier spectrum increases with re-uploading depth L up to an optimal bound, beyond which gradient variance decays (barren plateau effect) and causes training stagnation or overfitting on validation folds.

hypotheses.title: Clinical interpretability via analytical gradients
hypotheses.statement: Analytical gradient saliency derived from the classical backbone and quantum parameter-shift rule concentrates its mass on electrophysiologically relevant fronto-central channels and Theta/Beta frequency components rather than posterior noise.

hypotheses.title: Controlled synthetic capacity and robustness
hypotheses.statement: With a fixed feature front end, the re-uploading readout (L=3) represents a class rule needing Fourier frequency two in one feature, which single-shot angle encoding (L=1) cannot; under a monotone class signal every arm stays near the known ceiling, and its degradation with label noise is measured.

central.text: Degraded subject-level classification accuracy of hybrid quantum-classical models with shallow data encodings on pediatric ADHD EEG.

causes.text: High inter-subject variability, low signal-to-noise ratio and volume-conduction blurring in multichannel EEG recordings.
Restricted expressivity of single-shot quantum encodings and vanishing gradients in deeper parameterized circuits.
Overestimated generalization from small clinical cohorts when epochs of one subject leak across data splits.

effects.text: Unreliable subject-independent ADHD screening on unseen children.
Inconsistent gains of quantum layers over classical EEG baselines.
Inflated circuit depth and unstable training in hybrid classifiers.

layers.name: Layer 1: EEG inputs
layers.desc: Epochs $X \in \mathbb{R}^{C \times T}$ with $C = 19$ channels of the 10-20 montage; subjects labeled ADHD ($y = 1$) or healthy control ($y = 0$).

nodes.name: 10-20 montage
nodes.desc: Standardized electrode positions, fronto-central sites included

nodes.name: Subject label
nodes.desc: $y_s \in \{0, 1\}$ shared by all the subject's epochs

layers.name: Layer 2: Classical spatial-temporal backbone
layers.desc: Convolutional encoder $f_{\phi}$ bounded by a scaled tanh to the rotation domain (Eq. 1).

nodes.name: Generic features
nodes.desc: No physiological meaning imposed; biomarkers are contrasted post hoc

layers.name: Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circuit
layers.desc: $L$ layers of encoding and variational blocks on $N_q = 4$ qubits (Eqs. 2-5).

layers.name: Layer 4: Readout and objective
layers.desc: Pauli-Z expectations, a linear readout with a sigmoid, and a subject-weighted loss (Eqs. 6-8).

nodes.name: Subject-weighted BCE
nodes.desc: Each subject weighs the same; $\lambda_w \|w\|_2^2$ on the readout, weight decay $\lambda_{\phi}$ on the backbone, no penalty on $\theta$

layers.name: Layer 5: Clinical interpretability
layers.desc: Channel-time saliency from exact gradients through both stages (Eq. 9).

nodes.name: Quantum gradients
nodes.desc: $\partial \hat{y} / \partial x_k$ by backpropagation in simulation, parameter shift on hardware

nodes.name: Saliency map
nodes.desc: $\mathcal{I}(c, t)$ per electrode and time sample

nodes.name: Biomarker contrast
nodes.desc: Post-hoc comparison of the learned features with Theta, Beta, TBR and frontal coherence

contribution_type.why: The revision is built around one real clinical use case, subject-independent pediatric ADHD screening from 19-channel 10-20 EEG on the IEEE Dataport cohort. Its design follows from that case: a subject-weighted loss (Eq. 8) against cross-subject leakage (DC3), and fronto-central saliency for a clinical audit (Eq. 9, E4). Its mathematics reuses known results (data re-uploading, the Schuld et al. Fourier spectrum, Eqs. 2-5) rather than proving new ones.

General.why: E1-E3 test a general hybrid design question (re-uploading vs. single-shot encoding, ring vs. linear entanglement, depth vs. barren plateaus), but they are only tested on one clinical dataset, so the claims are narrower than a General contribution.

Theory.why: The Fourier spectrum of degree L (Section 3.2) and the bipartition limit (Higuchi-Sudbery) are cited, not proved. No hypothesis E1-E5 proposes a theorem or a new proof technique.

Use-Inspired.why: The use case is real (ADHD diagnosis biased by questionnaires) and the design fits it (Eqs. 8-9, E4 checks against the TBR biomarker). But E1 compares only with ML baselines; no non-ML clinical rule, such as a Theta/Beta ratio threshold, is planned.

Concept & Feasibility.why: A 4-qubit simulated pilot on 121 subjects with a synthetic capacity test (E5) reads as feasibility. But data re-uploading is an existing idea, so the type's high bar (an idea that changes how the problem is approached) is not met.

Negative Results.why: Every hypothesis E1-E5 predicts a positive effect. Only E3 expects gradient decay beyond some depth, and that is a planned ablation, not a central negative finding grounded in deeper analysis.
